items.text: The runnable revision 57 cycle-control model proves sequential escrow isolation, reconciliation-first restart, and failure-bound fresh-cycle recovery

The owner-approved per-cycle survivability bounds keep contamination and blind-retry mutation at zero, one active cycle, distinct escrows, and a 100 USDG authorized-loss cap without claiming a cumulative system cap
External-service spikes for unproven integrations ran (or the owner explicitly waived them)
Interfaces frozen NOW: freeze receipt binds final interface hashes; architecture receipt re-checked against them
Any unsupported delta from certified modules escalated the risk lane

redFlags: A model whose inputs are all optimistic
Expected-value arithmetic used to prove solvency (EV cannot establish solvency)
Freeze receipt created before the model ran

rationalizations.excuse: The worst case won't actually happen
rationalizations.reality: The worst case is the only scenario the model exists for. If it is unsurvivable, redesign now — it is cheap here and expensive live.
